Note: A Preposition is a word placed before a noun or a pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition) and shows a relationship in space or time or a logical relationship between two or more people, places, or things in a sentence.

Examples

I. The teacher scolded the child for being late.

II. We're going to a party.

· The words in bold are called prepositions because they normally take position before (pre) a noun/pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition.

· The noun/pronoun which is used with a preposition is called its Object.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Rehan and Ronit are / good friends and / it don't matter to them / as to who is wealthier.

questions.question: Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order. The rattlesnake P. it has specialized Jacobson's Q. organ, which gives it a heightened R. knows when to lie low because S. sense of smell to detect prey
questions.questionHtml:

The rattlesnake

P. it has specialized Jacobson's

Q. organ, which gives it a heightened

R. knows when to lie low because

S. sense of smell to detect prey
questions.solution:
The phrase "the rattlesnake" will be followed by part R as it helps introduce the fact about the subject.

PQ forms a pair as it talks about 'Jacobson's organ'. PQ follows R as PQ gives the reason as to why the rattlesnake lies low.

S concludes the sentence as it states how the Jacobson's organ helps the snake [by enhancing its sense of smell].

So, the correct order is: RPQS.

The correct sentence is: The rattlesnake knows when to lie low because it has specialized Jacobson's organ, which gives it a heightened sense of smell to detect prey.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the correct indirect from of the given sentence. She said to me, "The charlatan will be breaking into the safe."
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct indirect from of the given sentence.

She said to me, "The charlatan will be breaking into the safe."

options.text: She told me that the charlatan would be breaking into the safe.
options.html: She told me that the charlatan would be breaking into the safe.

options.text: She said to me that the charlatan will be breaking in the safe.

options.text: She said to me that the charlatan will be breaking into the safe.

options.text: She said to me that the charlatan is breaking into the safe.
options.html: She said to me that the charlatan is breaking into the safe.

questions.solution:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Future Continuous Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Conditional Continuous.

Future Continuous (Subject + will/shall + be + V1 + ing + Object) should be converted into Conditional Continuous (Subject + would/should + be + V1 +ing + Object).

For example:

He said, "I will be using the book next Friday." (Direct Speech)

He said that he would be using the book the following Friday. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

DIRECT

INDIRECT
Said toTold
WillWould

Therefore, the correct answer is option (a): She told me that the charlatan would be breaking into the safe.

questions.question: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. Shalu has ordered new copies of the album.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

Shalu has ordered new copies of the album.

options.text: New copies of the album have being ordered by Shalu.
options.html: New copies of the album have being ordered by Shalu.

options.html: New copies of the album has been order by Shalu.

options.text: New copies of the album have been ordered by Shalu.
options.html: New copies of the album have been ordered by Shalu.

questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb ['been' for the given sentence] is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Present Perfect. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Present Perfect.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + has/have + V3 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + has/have + been + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

Arya has bought a new horse. (Active Voice)

A new horse has been bought by Arya. (Passive Voice)

The options except (d) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (d): New copies of the album have been ordered by Shalu.

Note: Since 'new copies of the album' is the plural subject, the plural verb 'have' should follow [and not the singular verb 'has'].

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.

questions.solution:
The sentence implies that people associated with the game get so excited. 'Campaigners' and 'reformers' do not fit in contextually.

'Champions' can fit in the blank, but 'supporters' is the more wider term and encompass more number of people to be excited about the game.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.solution:
The sentence implies that generally people associated with the game become so excited and it may lead to chaos, confusion and riots.

'Adapt' means 'become adjusted to new condition'. It is incorrect as the verb is followed by the preposition 'to' [not 'into'].

'Reshape' means 'shape or form (something) differently or again'. It also does not form a correct phrase with the preposition 'into'.

'Transfigure' means 'transform into something more beautiful or elevate'. It does not fit in contextually as riots are not beautiful, they have adverse consequences.

'Convert' means 'change the form, character, or function of something'.

It can be followed by the preposition 'into'.

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.solution:
The preposition used after the blank is 'in'. When talking about places, 'in' is used to indicate a location or place.

A route/track is not a place in which the racing could take place [though the path on which the racing is done is called track].

The most appropriate word to fill the blank is 'stadium'. Stadium is a place in which the track/route can be carved and racing competition can be conducted.

'Circuit' does not fit in contextually.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.solution:
Here, the superlative degree of adjective should be used as the sentence informs about 'Circus' which was superior in a way than all others in Rome.

Now, the sentence mentions that it could hold 3,85,000 spectators. It does not have anything to do with the height of the 'Circus', but its size.

The adjective 'largest' can be used to denote this.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

Note: · The Positive Degree of an Adjective is the Adjective in its simple form. It is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree of an adjective denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.
